+description: Learn how you can add the Appwrite MCP server to Pi to interact with both the Appwrite API and documentation, and to react to events in your project.
+Get started quickly with these pre-built prompts for common Appwrite integrations:
+{% section #step-2 step=2 title="Add the MCP server" %}

+Connect the Appwrite MCP server to [Pi](https://pi.dev), a terminal coding agent, for deeper integration with the Appwrite API and documentation. It is a remote HTTP server, so you only need Pi itself.
+If you don't have Pi yet, install it from your terminal. See [pi.dev](https://pi.dev) for other ways to install it, such as npm.
+Pi connects to the server through [pi-mcp-adapter](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter), a Pi extension that adds MCP servers to your sessions. Install it:

+The server uses OAuth for authentication. Start Pi by running `pi` in your terminal, then run `/mcp-auth appwrite`. Your browser opens so you can sign in to your Appwrite account and authorize access. Pi stores the sign-in in your operating system's credential store, so you don't need an API key.

+Pi can also add MCP servers with `pi mcp add`. The events extension in [Step 4](#step-4) works only with pi-mcp-adapter, so this guide uses the adapter. The adapter turns off Pi's built-in MCP support in Pi's settings, so the two don't both run.
+Run `/mcp` in Pi to check that **appwrite** is listed with its tools. Then try out the following example prompts:
+- `Create a new user in my Appwrite project`
+- `Show me the tables in my database`
+- `How do I set up real-time subscriptions in Appwrite?`
+- `Show me how to authenticate users with OAuth`
+- `How do I implement file uploads with Appwrite Storage?`
+{% section #step-4 step=4 title="React to project events" %}

+The Appwrite MCP server supports [MCP Events](/docs/tooling/ai/mcp-servers#events), an MCP extension that lets an agent subscribe to changes in your project. Pi can subscribe to an event, such as a new user, finish its turn, and wake up when the event happens. The server pushes each event over the connection Pi already has open, so you don't need a public URL.
+Pi receives events through [pi-mcp-events](https://github.com/mikekelly/pi-mcp-events), an extension that adds an `mcp_events` tool on top of pi-mcp-adapter. Install it, then restart Pi to load it:
+Ask Pi to subscribe to `users.user.created`. Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` with your project ID:

+Subscribe with mcp_events to users.user.created on the appwrite server for project_id <PROJECT_ID>, then finish your turn and wait. Whenever an event arrives, look up that user and tell me their name and email.
+Pi opens the subscription and goes idle.
+When a user signs up or you create one in the Appwrite Console, Pi wakes up without a new prompt, looks up the user, and replies with their name and email.
+Each subscription is a webhook in your project, so it counts toward your plan's webhook limit. When you no longer need the events, ask Pi to unsubscribe:

+Subscriptions last as long as the Pi session. After you restart Pi, ask it to subscribe again. To see every event you can subscribe to and how delivery works, read [Events](/docs/tooling/ai/mcp-servers#events).

+- Antigravity, Zed, OpenCode, Grok Build, and Pi have their own sections. Anything else: **Other agents**.
If you still cannot tell, ask the user one question: which app are they using?
For the user's list: start a new Grok session, run \`/mcps\`, select **appwrite**, and press \`i\` to sign in.
+Pi connects to MCP servers through the \`pi-mcp-adapter\` extension. Install it and the skills:
+For the user's list: restart Pi, run \`/mcp-auth ${MCP_SERVER_NAME}\`, and approve the sign-in in the browser.

Add a remote HTTP server named \`${MCP_SERVER_NAME}\` with URL \`${MCP_SERVER_URL}\` to your app's user-level MCP configuration, and install the skills with \`npx --yes skills add appwrite/skills -g -s '*' -y\` (add \`-a <agent>\` when the skills CLI knows your app). Clients that only support stdio can run the server through \`npx mcp-remote ${MCP_SERVER_URL}\`.
